name: Indonesia

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 87%, Christian about 10%, Hindu in Bali

snapshot: Fuel price rises triggered by the Iran war brought students back onto the streets against Prabowo Subianto, whose free school meals programme has become a lightning rod.
culture: Indonesia's motto is "Unity in Diversity", for some 1,300 ethnic groups across 17,000 islands. Bahasa Indonesia, deliberately chosen as a neutral language, unites them. Javanese gamelan, wayang shadow puppetry and batik are UNESCO-listed, and Bali's Hindu culture draws millions of tourists. Badminton is a national passion.
society: Indonesia is the world's largest Muslim-majority democracy and Southeast Asia's biggest economy. It dominates global nickel supply for electric car batteries after banning raw ore exports. Jakarta is sinking, and a new capital, Nusantara, is being built in Borneo. Deforestation for palm oil and mining remains a concern.
situation: Prabowo Subianto, a former general once banned from the United States over human rights abuses under the Suharto dictatorship, won Indonesia's presidency in 2024 promising to feed every schoolchild. His free school meals programme, costing tens of billions of dollars, became the centrepiece of his government. In 2026 it also became a symbol of everything his critics dislike about it.

As the Iran war sent oil prices soaring, Prabowo's government raised prices of non-subsidised petrol by about 30 percent in June to ease pressure on the budget. Students marched in Jakarta and other cities, demanding a reversal and an end to the meals scheme, which has been criticised as wasteful and linked to mass food poisonings; in Surabaya, police arrested 24 protesters after clashes (AFP via Gulf Times). Protesters also objected to the growing role of the military in civilian life. The unrest echoed the August-September 2025 protests over lavish perks for lawmakers, Prabowo's worst crisis so far, which left 10 dead and thousands arrested. For the world's fourth most populous country, the question is whether a president with a huge parliamentary coalition and an authoritarian past will bend to street pressure or harden.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years with a two-term limit and heads the government; the House of Representatives and a regional chamber make up the legislature. Prabowo's coalition controls most of parliament.
holders: President Prabowo Subianto, since October 2024; the vice presidency is vacant since Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on 12 November 2026.

update.html: On 12 November Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of former president Joko Widodo, resigned after the Constitutional Court and Supreme Court ruled in October that his school credentials did not meet the requirements to run, and hours before the House was to take up an impeachment petition signed by more than 120 lawmakers. Prabowo accepted the resignation; the post stays vacant until the People's Consultative Assembly picks a successor from two presidential nominees within 60 days. Earlier, on 3 November, police arrested Prabowo's chief of staff and former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo on suspicion of wiretapping the president.
